chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The memoriser of the Quran, the one who acts by it, will be with the Ambassadors (angelic scribes), the honourable, the righteous.

key_terms.السَّفَرَةُ الْكِرَامُ الْبَرَرَةُ: The honourable and righteous scribes — angelic beings referenced in Surah 'Abasa (80:15-16) who record and carry divine messages
key_terms.الْحَافِظُ: One who preserves and memorises the Quran (hafiz); in Islamic tradition, this carries both intellectual mastery and spiritual responsibility
key_terms.الْعَامِلُ بِهِ: The one who acts by it — emphasising that memorisation alone is insufficient; righteous action is required

ai.seo_question: What reward does a Quran memoriser who acts by it receive according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) promises that the person who memorises the Quran and puts it into practice will be in the company of the noble angelic scribes on the Day of Judgment. The term 'al-safarah' refers to the angelic scribes mentioned in Quran 80:15-16, described as honourable and righteous. This teaching was addressed to the early Shia community to encourage not merely memorisation of the Quran but active implementation of its teachings in daily life.
